extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors, peer reviewers, and editorial board members of the Turkish Journal of Emergency Medicine
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial and publication standards and requirements for submitting, reviewing, and publishing manuscripts in the Turkish Journal of Emergency Medicine, covering authorship, conflicts of interest, ethics, data sharing, corrections/retractions, AI use, and misconduct policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to recognized editorial and reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Turk J Emerg Med follows the suggestions, policies, and checklists of CSE, WAME, COPE, ICMJE, and the EQUATOR network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and editors are expected to follow these external bodies' recommendations and checklists for reporting and editorial independence; peer-reviewers are asked to consider ethical/reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each author, reviewer, and editor must disclose any conflict of interest related to family, personal, financial, political, or religious issues and any competing interest as defined by WAME.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer, associate editor, or editor has a conflict of interest or believes it is inappropriate to act, they should resign from the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria (ICMJE four conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship credit requires: (1) substantial contributions to conception/design or acquisition/analysis/interpretation of data; (2) drafting or critical revision for important intellectual content; (3) final approval of the version published; (4) agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All four conditions must be met. Each author should identify co-authors responsible for specific parts. Participation solely in funding acquisition, data collection, or general supervision does not justify authorship. A contributorship statement is required. Any change to authors after submission must be explained and approved by the Editor; the Editor may contact authors to verify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributorship statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: A contributorship statement is required for every manuscript and should outline who contributed to planning, conduct, and reporting of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List contributors who do not meet authorship criteria in the Acknowledgements and ensure they have granted permission to be listed (examples: supervision, administrative support, writing assistance, technical/language editing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for submissions from Editorial Board members
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions from Editorial Board members undergo a double-blind peer review, are managed by an independent editor with no conflict, and board members may publish up to three articles per calendar year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity of authors and reviewers is concealed; independent editor oversees reviewer selection and final decision to avoid bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author conflict of interest disclosure (ICMJE uniform declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should disclose: (1) associations with commercial entities that provided support for the work (timeframe = lifespan of the work); (2) associations with entities that could be viewed as having an interest in the general area (timeframe = 36 months before submission); (3) similar financial associations of spouse/children under 18; (4) non-financial associations relevant to the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests will be declared in the published article; they are not automatic grounds for rejection. Examples include board membership, consultancy, employment, grants (including pending), contract research, lectures, patents, equipment receipts, royalties, stock/options, and other personal/professional relationships. The corresponding author must include a summary COI statement in the First Pages File; default published statement if none is 'None declared'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and reuse license
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal grants free, irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual right of access and a license to copy, use, distribute, perform and display the work publicly and to make/distribute derivative works in any digital medium for any reasonable non-commercial purpose, subject to proper attribution. Small printed copies for personal non-commercial use are allowed under Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 4.0 International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal content is protected under Indian and international copyrights but is made available under the stated CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI-assisted technologies disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If artificial intelligence-assisted technology was used anywhere in the article, it must be mentioned on the First Page in a new section and will appear in the published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a statement such as: 'During the preparation of this work, the author(s) used [NAME OF THE TOOL] ... After using this tool/service, the author(s) reviewed and edited the content as needed and take(s) full responsibility for the content.' Note: AI technologies cannot be used to change the content of images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections (Errata) policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors detected after publication require publication of a correction; minor corrections that do not affect scientific understanding may be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an article has appeared in an issue, an Erratum may be printed in the next available issue with reciprocal linking between online versions; the publisher may correct the online pdf and xml with a note describing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction and expression of concern policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors consider retractions for unreliable data/findings, plagiarism, duplicate publication, and unethical research; expression of concern may be used if an article is under investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All retraction notices explain why the paper was retracted. A replacement version containing metadata with a retraction note will be posted; PDF will be watermarked 'Retracted' while original text remains accessible. In rare legal-removal cases, original content may be removed and replaced with a legal note; a retraction notice will be published online and in the next print issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing encouragement and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to make the full data sets underlying their article openly and publicly available upon publication (data deposition is not considered prior publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend recognized repositories (OSF, Figshare, Zenodo, Dryad, fairsharing, re3data.org). If data are shared, cite them in the reference list per DataCite format: Creator (PublicationYear). Title. Version. Publisher. ResourceType. Identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data availability statement templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must create a Data Availability Statement indicating whether data are in a public repository, available on request, or obtained from a third party and not public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide repository name, persistent URL, and any reuse conditions for public data. For 'available upon request', state what the data are and who they are available from with publishable contact details and conditions. For third-party non-public data, state what the data are, the source, contact details, and conditions of reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources of funding should be declared under the heading 'Funding' in the First Pages File.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must describe the role of study sponsor(s) in study design, data collection/analysis/interpretation, reporting, and decision to submit. If funders had no involvement, that should be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandated ORCID iDs for submitting and co-authors
rubrics_metrics.description: ORCID iDs are mandated for all submitting and co-authors to disambiguate researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will be asked to provide ORCID along with name, e-mail, and institutional affiliation on submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patient consent for identifiable living individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Any article containing personal medical information about an identifiable living individual requires the patient's explicit consent before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consent may be any form in the patient's language declaring awareness of publication and use of data; when obtained it will be indicated in the published article. If consent cannot be obtained because the patient cannot be traced, publication is only possible with local Ethics Committee approval and sufficient anonymization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent and publication considerations for patients who lack capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patient lacks the mental capacity to decide on publication, no one can consent on their behalf except when done in the patient's best interests; often personal information should be anonymized or not published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor will generally require anonymization or may decline publication; assess possible future harm to the individual when published as a minor or incapacitated person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent for deceased patients
rubrics_metrics.description: For deceased patients, authors should seek permission from next of kin as a matter of courtesy and medical ethics; if relatives are not contactable, publication only possible by local Ethics Committee approval and signed author declaration for legal accountability under Turkish law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Turkish Law on Regulation On Personal Health Data (21.06.2019, Legal Gazette no:30808) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent for minors (children)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patient is under 18, parents or guardians must provide consent; if the child has sufficient understanding, the child must also sign the consent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with parental consent, consider whether the child might regret publication later; final decision rests with the journal editor who will consider possible future damage to the minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patient images and imaging consent
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patient may be identified from a photograph or image or its legend/text, the patient's written consent to publication is required; explicit permission required when face is clearly visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images such as x-rays, laparoscopic, ultrasound, pathology slides, or images of undistinctive body parts may be used without consent if anonymized by removing identifying marks and not accompanied by text that could reveal identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An anonymized article must not include any direct identifier (patient’s name, geographic location such as village or town, exact age, identity numbers, biometric data, photographs, and images including identifiable facial features).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure images and accompanying text do not allow identification; follow the instructions above for image anonymization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approval statement for human research
rubrics_metrics.description: Every research article including retrospective studies must include a statement that the study obtained ethics approval (or a statement that it was not needed and why), naming the ethics committee/IRB, approval number/ID and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For experimental research on humans include a statement that participants gave informed consent before taking part following detailed explanation of procedures. If ethical detail does not fit in the manuscript, provide it in the cover letter or as a supplemental file; peer-reviewers are asked to consider ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approval and standards for animal research
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts involving animals will be considered only if the work follows international, national and institutional guidelines for humane treatment, has ethics committee approval where such a committee exists, and complies with relevant legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-human primates demonstrate compliance with NC3Rs primates guidelines; for client-owned animals show high standard of veterinary care and informed client consent. Authors must confirm legal and ethical requirements have been met and specify ethical review committee approval process and guidelines followed in Methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling suspected unethical research or unethical submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Editor considers submitted work ethically unsound, they may seek advice, recommend investigation/action, contact the department head, or write to the paper's guarantor or professional registration body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions may include recommending local investigation or contacting regulatory/professional bodies (e.g., Clinical Research Department of the Turkish Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency for Turkish physicians).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific misconduct — overview and case-by-case handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal follows COPE, WAME, and ICMJE guidance to deal with scientific misconduct on a case-by-case basis; misconduct behaviors include falsification, plagiarism, redundant/duplicate publication, simultaneous submission, improprieties of authorship, misappropriation of ideas, violations of accepted research practices, material failure to comply with laws/regulations, and inappropriate behavior about misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and examples: falsification ranges from fabrication to dishonest reporting or omission; plagiarism is appropriation of language/ideas without credit; simultaneous submission is sending a paper to multiple journals at once; improprieties of authorship include excluding others or including undeserving authors; misappropriation can occur via review processes; violations include deceptive statistics or lack of transparency. The editorial team will assess and act according to guidance from COPE/WAME/ORI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salami slicing (redundant publication) prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Salami slicing (unnecessary splitting of findings from a single study across several publications) is considered redundant publication and is not accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted articles will be assessed for potential salami-slicing during standard checks. Studies sharing significant similarities in hypotheses, population, and methods should usually be presented in a single paper. If authors believe multiple publications are justified they should inform the editorial office about all potentially overlapping papers (published or unpublished). Refer to ICMJE guidance on overlapping publications for best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism detection and screening
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted manuscripts are screened with iThenticate (CrossCheck) to detect overlapping and similar text instances; high similarity scores may lead to rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases of suspected plagiarism the manuscript will be immediately rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission implies that the work has not been accepted for publication elsewhere, is not under consideration elsewhere, and does not duplicate material already published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to disclose any related papers in press, including translations. This restriction does not apply to abstracts presented at meetings/congresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial registration encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal encourages authors to register clinical trials to ensure thorough and transparent reporting; WHO has developed a minimum dataset and a portal linking to major registries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration helps ensure registries include consistent information; authors are encouraged to register their studies (implied expectation for clinical trials).
